questions.stem: A student needs to obtain pure water from seawater. Which separation technique should they use?

options.text: Filtration
Evaporation
Simple distillation
Chromatography

questions.explanation: Simple distillation heats the seawater to boil off the water, then condenses the steam back to pure liquid water in a separate container. Filtration cannot separate dissolved salt from water. Evaporation would give the salt, not the water. Chromatography is used for separating dissolved substances like dyes.

questions.stem: A mixture contains sand and salt. Which combination of techniques would separate them into pure sand and pure salt?

options.text: Dissolve in water, filter to get sand, evaporate filtrate to get salt
Heat the mixture to melt the salt, then pour off the liquid
Use a magnet to attract the sand, leaving the salt
Use chromatography to separate the two substances

questions.explanation: First, add water to dissolve the salt (salt is soluble, sand is not). Filter the mixture: sand stays in the filter paper as the residue, and salt solution passes through as the filtrate. Evaporate the filtrate to crystallise the pure salt. This uses differences in solubility to achieve separation.

questions.stem: Fractional distillation is used instead of simple distillation when:

options.text: Separating an insoluble solid from a liquid
Separating two or more liquids with different boiling points
Separating a dissolved solid from a solution
Separating different coloured dyes

questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids (liquids that mix) with different boiling points. The fractionating column provides a temperature gradient, allowing each liquid to be collected at its boiling point. This is used to separate crude oil into fractions and to separate ethanol from water.

questions.stem: A chromatography experiment shows that a food dye produces three spots on the chromatogram. What does this tell you?

options.text: The food dye is a pure substance
The food dye contains three different substances
The food dye has three different colours
The experiment has been done incorrectly

questions.explanation: In chromatography, each spot represents a different substance. Three spots indicate the food dye is a mixture of three different substances (dyes). A pure substance would produce only one spot. The substances separate because they have different solubilities in the solvent and different attractions to the paper.

questions.stem: Which separation technique relies on differences in boiling point?

options.text: Filtration
Chromatography
Distillation
Crystallisation

questions.explanation: Distillation (both simple and fractional) relies on substances having different boiling points. The liquid with the lowest boiling point evaporates first and is collected by condensation. Filtration separates by particle size, chromatography by solubility and attraction to the stationary phase, and crystallisation by solubility differences at different temperatures.
